question: Does among-radiation variation in hidden fine-state memory covary with how much exact fine flower-colour identity persists across relative evolutionary divergence?

analysis_frame.included_units: intersection of the 21 existing hidden-memory opportunity clades and the 28 historical common-frame persistence clades

primary_hypothesis.rationale: If stronger hidden fine-state organization reflects more persistent exact fine-colour identity through relative evolutionary divergence, clades with greater integrated fine-colour excess-retention area should show stronger hidden-memory effects.
primary_hypothesis.test: Spearman rho with 99999 two-sided label permutations

secondary_rule: Secondary relations are descriptive only and cannot rescue a failed primary hypothesis or replace fine_area as the frozen primary predictor.
interpretation_if_supported: Hierarchical hidden memory covaries with the relative evolutionary persistence of exact fine flower-colour identity, linking nested within-coarse organization to a temporal persistence axis.
interpretation_if_not_supported: Hierarchical hidden memory is not reducible to greater integrated fine-colour persistence through relative divergence; within-coarse organization and global fine-state persistence remain separable evolutionary axes.
boundaries: post-outcome exploratory because both component outcomes already exist
shared source states and phylogenies mean this is not independent replication
relative divergence depth only; no absolute-time claim
persistence area is a derived same-state summary, not a transition-rate estimate
secondary relations cannot replace the primary test
no ecological or molecular cause inferred
